title: Sensitivity
body:
$$
\text{Sensitivity} = \frac{\text{TP}}{\text{TP} + \text{FN}}
$$

**Of the things that really were positive, what fraction did you catch?** Three names for one
quantity: sensitivity (medicine), recall (information retrieval), true positive rate (signal
detection and ROC curves). All three are this formula.

It is computed **down the truth column** of the [[Confusion Matrix]], so its denominator is every
real positive and nothing else. That is what makes it immune to the base rate: adding a million
easy negatives to the test set does not move it, which is exactly why it is reported instead of
accuracy on imbalanced data.

**In [[STATISTICS]] this is statistical power, $1-\beta$.** See [[Type I and Type II Errors]],
which owns that translation and the trade-off argument.

## Do not confuse it with precision

The commonest mistake in the whole vocabulary, because both start at [[True Positive]]:

| | Formula | Question | Denominator runs over |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Sensitivity / recall** | $\text{TP}/(\text{TP}+\text{FN})$ | did you find them all? | what is really positive |
| **Precision** | $\text{TP}/(\text{TP}+\text{FP})$ | were your calls right? | what you called positive |

Either one alone is trivially gamed: predict positive for everything and recall is 100%; predict
positive once, on your most confident case, and precision is 100%. They are reported together for
that reason, and the F1 score is their harmonic mean, which is low unless both are decent.

## The trade-off

Lowering the decision threshold raises this and lowers [[Specificity]], every time. An ROC curve
plots one against the other across all thresholds, so it is $1-\beta$ against $\alpha$ drawn as a
curve. The only thing that improves both at once is more data.

## Related

- [[Specificity]]: the mirror image, computed down the negative column
- [[Confusion Matrix]], [[True Positive]], [[False Negative]]
- [[Type I and Type II Errors]] ([[STATISTICS]]): the same quantity as power
- [[Stratification]]: keeping the test split honest enough for this to mean anything
